newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent firms again, other grades at stalemate.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent firms again, other grades at stalemate.

text.p: Dated Brent crude firmed for a second day running on Tuesday, as a trader/refiner continued to cover commitments into the U.S. Gulf for late June arrival, traders said.
A June 4-6 cargo kept from the paper chains on Tuesday fetched July Brent -10 cents, 10 cents more than the same buyer paid for a June 3-5 cargo on Monday.
Traders said this week's buyer may still need another cargo to cover sales for June 22-27 arrival and for its own system.
One million barrels of prompter May 27-29 Brent traded earlier at a cheaper July Brent -25 cents, they said.
Brent CFDs jumped about six cents after news of the firmer Dated Brent deal, with the balance of this week talked at July Brent -15/-12 cents and the May 27-30 period at -16/-14 cents.
But other North Sea markets were at a stalemate, with buyers unwilling to contemplate the stronger differentials on offer against a background of poor refining margins, trader said.
"This is a difficult market to trade. Physical is tight but with the margins nobody is rushing to do anything," said one.
"We are waiting to buy but the margins are very poor, for topping they're even negative, and the high freight rates are also holding us back," said a refinery trader.
In the Mediterranean, at least eight Urals cargoes, mostly end May, were on offer but none seemed to have been taken.
Buyers, hurt by negative refining margins due to Brent's recent rise, were waiting for any signs of improvement before buying the sour crude, traders said.

One refiner said buyers and sellers were at Dated Brent -$1.15/$1.10 and -$1.20/$1.25 respectively, but another trader said although end May barrels could be picked up at a $1.20 discount, later barrels could fetch higher prices.
"There's lots of cargoes with question marks on them. This will put pressure on prices," one refiner said.
